claim: Coverage (any sample correct) rises roughly log-linearly with number of samples over orders of magnitude (Gemma-2B CodeContests 0.02% to 7.1% at 10,000; Llama-3-8B MATH 82.9% to 98.44%).
agent_test: Measure coverage vs N on our task set at fixed token budgets; fit curve; find N where gain per token falls below threshold.

claim: Selection is the bottleneck: with no ground-truth verifier, majority vote or reward model plateaus (MATH Llama-3-8B 40.50% to 41.41% from 100 to 10,000 samples) while coverage reaches 98%.
agent_test: Compare oracle-pick vs our selector at equal N; report the gap.

claim: With an automatic verifier, many cheap samples beat one strong sample (DeepSeek-Coder-V2 SWE-bench Lite 15.9% at 1 to 56% at 250 vs SOTA 43%). Caveat (d08): on SWE-bench Verified, generated tests and a trained scorer each saturate at 42-43%; the combination reaches 51%.
agent_test: Only use sample-heavy mode on items with a runnable check (code, math with answer check).

claim: Imperfect verifiers cap resampling: with non-zero false-positive rate accuracy has a ceiling, and optimal attempts are often under 10. New (d06, d08): self-verifiers also have high false-negative rates on planning tasks (GPT-4 95.8-97% on two domains) and generated tests separate patches poorly.
agent_test: Estimate verifier false-positive rate per task type; cap N at the cost-optimal value.

claim: Optimal compute allocation depends on difficulty: easy items gain from sequential revision, hard ones from parallel sampling or search; oracle-bin adaptive allocation matches best-of-N with about 4x less compute (PaLM 2-S*, MATH). With a learned difficulty predictor, a second group saw 25-50% savings on math and code (up to 50%), 0-10% on chat, and 25-40% fewer calls for model routing; the oracle curve stays above the predictor.
agent_test: Gate by predicted difficulty (pass-rate on a few cheap samples) and compare to uniform N at equal total tokens. Note Snell is one model family and one benchmark.

claim: The best search method depends on policy size, PRM and difficulty; Snell's difficulty-bin recipe does not transfer unchanged (small models best-of-N easy / beam hard; 72B best-of-N everywhere).
agent_test: Do not hard-code a search method; calibrate on our model and verifier.

claim: Smaller model plus more samples or better search can beat a larger model at equal FLOPs until the small model saturates (Llemma-7B beats 34B up to 128 samples; REBASE; Snell 14x comparison on easy/medium items). Correction from cross-check: the 'about 2x fewer FLOPs' for Llemma-7B+REBASE vs 34B is unverified; the paper states 7 times less compute for REBASE vs weighted voting on the 7B model.
agent_test: Equal-FLOPs comparison of small-model-many-samples vs large-model-one-shot on our items, split by difficulty.

claim: Headline claims that 1B beats 405B or 7B beats o1 (Liu et al.) are author-reported and rely on a strong PRM at large N; treat as upper bound, not as default.
agent_test: Replicate on one pair with our own verifier before relying on it.

claim: Sequential vs parallel scaling is unresolved: s1 finds budget forcing beats majority vote; Wu 2025 and Zeng 2025 find parallel beats extended thinking at equal tokens; Snell says it depends on difficulty. New (d01, d02): Ghosal 2025 (small distilled models, forced 'Wait'): parallel +22% at 16K tokens; Sharma 2025 (open instruct models, refinement with feedback, 4096-token chain cap): sequential wins 43 of 45 matched-token cells. The two use different meanings of sequential, so the conflict is partly definitional. No frontier thinking-model test split by difficulty found.
agent_test: At equal tokens run extend-thinking vs k parallel chains by difficulty bin.

claim: Longer thinking is not reliably better: within one question, correct chains tend to be shorter (shortest beats longest by up to 34.5 points, random by up to 18.8).
agent_test: Rank by length among parallel chains; use short-m@k as cheap selector.

claim: Accuracy can fall as test-time compute rises: majority vote non-monotone in calls; extended thinking raises variance then lowers accuracy; inverse scaling on designed tasks (Opus 4 near 100% to about 80%).
agent_test: Add a hard cap and a stop rule; test our agent on distractor tasks with growing budget.

claim: Reasoning models overspend on easy items (2+3: 1,953% more tokens; first solution holds 38.7% of tokens on ASDIV; early exit cuts CoT 19-80% at +0.3 to +5.0 accuracy; NoThinking 51.3 vs 28.9 on AMC23 at 700 tokens).
agent_test: S0 gate: route easy items to a no-thinking short path; measure accuracy and tokens vs always-think.

claim: Three-regime view (plain model equal or better at low complexity, thinking wins at medium, both fail at high) is contested: Lawsen attributes the collapse to output limits and impossible instances. Update: the original authors add a temperature-0 control and note River Crossing N=3 (11 moves) still fails, so token limits explain only part; Lawsen concedes some early stopping looks like choice. No independent re-run with fixed limits and solvable-only instances found.
agent_test: Check regime split on our items with output limits lifted before using it for gating.

claim: RL on verifiable rewards improves pass@1 but base models reach equal or higher pass@k at large k, so extra samples mostly find what the base model already knows.
agent_test: Compare pass@k curves of scaffold vs plain at k up to 64 on our tasks.

claim: Self-consistency and chain of thought are the base results: CoT PaLM-540B GSM8K 17.9 to 56.9; self-consistency +17.9 GSM8K; gains small for weaker models.
agent_test: Treat as baseline arm at equal tokens.

claim: Process reward models beat outcome reward models and majority vote for best-of-N (78.2 vs 72.4 vs 69.6 at N=1860 on MATH subset).
agent_test: Only worth it if a step verifier exists; otherwise use self-verification.

claim: Self-verification of many random samples scales (Gemini 1.5 Pro Verification@200 reaches 467/500 MATH vs 428 for o1-Preview), and verifier-free distillation falls behind verifier-based methods as budget grows.
agent_test: Self-verify top-k candidates; compare with majority vote at equal tokens.

claim: Trading train-time for test-time compute is old and stable: AlphaZero Hex, 10x train compute buys about 15x test compute.
agent_test: Not testable for a no-training scaffold; context only.

claim: Moving compute offline (sleep-time) cuts test-time cost about 5x at equal accuracy on stateful tasks (Stateful GSM-Symbolic and AIME; o1 showed little gain). Amortised over 10 related questions per context the cost per query falls 2.5x; with 2 questions per context it is less favourable. Gain grows with query predictability. In an agentic SWE case sleep-time won only at low test budgets.
agent_test: Test only when context is reused across 10 or more questions and queries are predictable from the context; compare to plain test-time at a high budget.

claim: Early stopping of sampling by consistency saves about 34% of samples (up to 43% GSM8K) at similar accuracy. Wider range (d13, d14, d15): confidence-filtered online stopping saved about 19% to 85% of tokens at similar or higher accuracy on open reasoning models; the 34% figure is from sample-count stopping.
agent_test: Adaptive N: stop when first k answers agree; compare tokens at equal accuracy.

claim: Difficulty can be predicted cheaply well enough to save compute, but not as well as an oracle: a learned predictor of marginal reward saves up to 50% on math and code at equal success, 0-10% on typical chat, and 25-50% of calls when routing between models.
agent_test: Train or prompt a difficulty predictor on our own logged items; report tokens saved at equal accuracy vs oracle bins and vs uniform N.

claim: LLM self-verification and intrinsic self-correction are unreliable on reasoning and planning tasks: GPT-4 critique collapses accuracy (e.g. Game of 24 5% to 3%), judge false positive rate 10.4% and false negatives up to 97% in some domains; CommonSenseQA drops 75.8 to 38.1 after GPT-3.5 self-correction. A sound external check restores gains.
agent_test: Measure our judge false positive and false negative rates per task type; only loop on revision when an external check or tool result exists.

claim: Test-time scaling transfers to tool-using agents but modestly: on GAIA (n=165) whole-trajectory best-of-N with list-wise selection lifts GPT-4.1 from 55.76 to 63.03; step-level beam/DVTS and reflect-every-step give no gain or lose; reflect-only-when-low-score helps slightly (56.36). SWE agents gain from 34.4% to 51% with hybrid verifiers.
agent_test: Reflect only on low-score steps; resample whole trajectories rather than every step; pair a test signal with a second selector.

claim: Confidence- and convergence-based stopping works on open reasoning models and reduces tokens a lot (DeepConf up to 84.7%, DEER 19-80%, answer-consistency over 40% on NaturalQuestions), but aggressive filtering can hurt through overconfident wrong answers (GPT-OSS-120B).
agent_test: Compare prompted interim-answer-stability stopping to fixed budget at equal accuracy; keep the conservative setting.

claim: Whether stop rules combine (confidence exit, short-m@k, consistency-based sample stopping) and which gives best accuracy per token across models has not been tested head to head; the answer-convergence paper lists combination as future work.
agent_test: Run the three rules alone and combined on one fixed item set at equal total tokens.

claim: Inverse scaling appears on designed tasks with five failure modes (distraction, framing overfit, spurious features, constraint-tracking loss, self-preservation drift). Few-shot examples largely fixed the spurious-feature mode; no study tested a budget cap or a distractor filter as a fix.
agent_test: Inject distractors into memory and long constraint tasks; compare uncapped, capped, and filtered runs.

claim: Independent replication of small-model-beats-large claims (Liu 2025) with a weak, non-ground-truth PRM was not found. Related evidence only: a label-free ensemble of weak verifiers lifts Llama 3.3 70B from first-sample to o3-mini level (87.7% vs 86.7%) at K=100, which is a different claim.
agent_test: Replicate one small/large pair with our own verifier before relying on it.
